14/G.goal: Describe the main hardware components of a VR system, including non-hand input methods, the processing component, and visual and non-visual output devices.
14/G.achieves: Provides the foundational XR hardware knowledge needed to understand, evaluate, and implement a VR system within the course's practical development approach.

14/O1.goal: Explain the non-hand input techniques used in VR, including the categories of full-body tracking and sound-based tracking.
14/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a basis for understanding how VR systems capture user motion and voice to support interaction, embodiment, and social presence in later XR design.

14/O2.goal: Describe the processing/computer component of a VR system, including selection factors and the roles of GPU, CPU, and RAM.
14/O2.achieves: Enables the learner to evaluate computing platforms and understand the hardware constraints of VR rendering and application development.

14/O3.goal: Describe the main VR output devices, covering visual displays and non-visual audio, haptic, and motion-based outputs.
14/O3.achieves: Helps the learner understand how output hardware shapes immersion, sensory feedback, and motion-related user experience for later XR optimization and implementation.
